open_points.subject: A18 next-backup inclusion versus excluded agent sessions
open_points.text: “a change committed while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the next” contradicts A18 rule 2: “A backup holds every record but the agent sessions (M06), which are removed from the copy before it is encrypted”
open_points.question: Does “a change” exclude changes to agent-session records, or must the next backup somehow contain those changes despite the rule that it contains no agent session?
options: The promise applies only to durable records that backups include.
The next backup must represent agent-session changes too.
The sentence means only that the next snapshot observes the then-current eligible store state, not that every concurrent change is present.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the promise to records eligible for backup and exclude all M06 changes.

witness.initial: Agent session S is registered and has no granted projects; a daily backup run has begun its snapshot copy.
events: While the copy is being made, the owner grants project P to session S and the transaction commits.
The owner restores that next backup outside Registry.
outcomes: Under the new sentence, the committed grant is in the next backup, so the restored store represents S with access to P.
Under A18 rule 2, the next backup contains no AgentSession record at all, so the restored store has neither S nor its grant.
witness.observer: The owner after restore, and Kernel when it attempts to read or use session S.

open_points.subject: A18 unconditional inclusion in the next backup
open_points.text: “a change committed while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the next” conflicts with “the days this rule and rule 5 leave without a kept backup are allowed”, “a failed or missed run lengthens that by the days until a run succeeds”, and the ordinary rules that may change or erase the committed state before another snapshot.
open_points.question: What does “the next” mean, and is it promising inclusion of the committed historical change or only a later snapshot of whatever state then exists?
options: The next scheduled run, even if it fails or keeps no backup.
The next successfully kept backup contains only the state current at its snapshot, so an intervening erasure or replacement may remove the earlier change.
Every concurrent committed change must remain representable until a later backup captures it.
open_points.default_guess: Read it as the next successfully kept backup observing the then-current eligible state, not as preserving every intervening historical change.

witness.initial: Daily backup B1 is being copied; archived project P still exists whole.
events: During B1, the owner deletes P whole and that transaction commits.
The following scheduled backup run is missed or fails.
Before the next successful run, the restored or otherwise current store history contains no P, as deletion requires.
outcomes: The changed sentence requires the deletion change to be “in the next” backup, which could mean the immediately scheduled run must exist and keep a backup.
The other A18 rules allow that run to be absent or failed; B2 merely snapshots the later current store and provides no record that P or its deletion ever existed beyond any surviving audit state.
witness.observer: The owner examining kept backups or restoring the next available successful backup.
